104.0.s.en: (1) God the Creator of heaven and earth

104.0.0.en: Bless the Lord, O my soul. O Lord my God, thou art very great; thou art clothed with honour and majesty.

104.0.1.en: 1- The Psalm begins with the praise of God when the writer of the Psalm calls his soul to bless God. The writer speaks proudly about God, so he says "my God", that is, there is a special relationship between him and God, and he says to Him "thou art very great", not in the sense that He has increased in greatness, for He is perfect in Himself from eternity, but He has become great in the eyes of the writer of the Psalm when he perceived His care and His power which created the world and cares for it to order it. And everyone who believes in God and is purified by repentance can perceive the greatness of God.

104.0.2.en: 2- The writer of the Psalm likens God to a great man who has put on majesty and honour, meaning the greatness of God that appears before people in His creation and His care for the world. Glory and majesty cling to Him as clothes cling to a person.

104.1.0.en: Who coverest thyself with light as with a garment: who stretchest out the heavens like a curtain:

104.1.1.en: Curtain: a piece of cloth or skin that is easily stretched out, like a tent or a veil.

104.1.2.en: 1- God is light and the source of all light, so the writer of the Psalm expresses this by saying "who coverest thyself with light", that is, light clings to Him, and He is the Creator of light. Also He created the heavens by His word with ease, as a person stretches out the curtain of a tent, that is, the cloth of the tent, with ease. And whoever believes in the great God, as in (v. 1), enjoys His light, and then His word, which works in him with ease.

104.1.3.en: 2- God's covering Himself with light points to the Incarnation of Christ in His pure body, that is, a body of light. As for us believers, we put on the light, that is, Christ, if we walk in His commandments. And light reveals everything, so God, who covers Himself with light, searches the hearts and reins, and nothing is hidden from Him. And He stretched out the heaven after He created light on the first day, to declare that although heaven is His dwelling, we human beings who live on the earth cannot see His light, but we see something of His light as much as we are able to bear. Now we see Him as in a mirror, but there in heaven we shall see Him face to face (1 Cor 13:12), that is, God reveals to us some of His light. And as much as we live with Him, He reveals to us the mysteries of His light, so we enjoy fellowship with Him.

104.1.4.en: 3- And God, who covers Himself with light, lit up the world when He created light, and consequently there could afterward be life for man and all creatures; and God also enlightens our hearts with the knowledge of Him, so we are filled with joy.

104.2.0.en: Who layeth the beams of his chambers in the waters: who maketh the clouds his chariot: who walketh upon the wings of the wind:

104.2.1.en: His chambers: the plural of "chamber", the upper room in the house; what is meant by it is heaven.

104.2.2.en: 1- The writer of the Psalm shows the greatness of God in His creation of the heaven, which is water in the form of vapor, and He made it a roof for the earth and for everything above it, man, animals and birds. God's power is manifested in His control of this water, which is the cloud, so it cannot condense and come down as rain except by His command, and in the amount that He wills for the benefit of man. Job speaks of the cloud, likening it to a waterskin full of water, which God holds in His hand so that the whole earth is not flooded (Job 26:8).

104.2.3.en: 2- God rides upon the cloud and walks upon the wind, which the writer here likens to wings, like the wings of a bird. For God is the Creator of all these and their Controller, and He rides above them or walks upon them.

104.2.4.en: And because of the greatness of the cloud and the mist, it represents the presence of God, for its height above the earth and its splendor, as the mist used to cover the tent of meeting, or the temple of Solomon, at the presence of God (Ex 20:

104.2.5.en: 21; 1 Kgs 8:12), and when God came down on the mountain and gave Moses the commandments and the Law (Deut 5:22).

104.2.6.en: 3- The clouds, that is, the mist, represent mystery, so they are a symbol of the sacraments of the Church, and the waters are the waters of Baptism, and the winds point to the Holy Spirit who works in the Church, the sacraments and the believers.

104.2.7.en: In sum, God, who in His thought is exalted above all, works in His children in the Church to fill them with His power and give them all their needs, so He makes His earthly children angels who live in heaven while they are on earth.

104.3.0.en: Who maketh his angels spirits; his ministers a flaming fire:

104.3.1.en: 1- God is the Creator of the angels, and He created them winds, that is, spirits with great abilities in understanding and movement. They are spirits who perceive God's love and greatness, so they praise Him always, obey Him, serve Him and take care of human beings according to His commands. They are spirits whom man does not see, but he feels their work.

104.3.2.en: 2- God also created the angels a flaming fire, and that by His fiery Holy Spirit, and they are aflame with the love of God and reject evil; for fire consumes impurities and thorns, which are a symbol of sin, and they carry out God's commands quickly like the flame of fire.

104.4.0.en: Who laid the foundations of the earth, that it should not be removed for ever.

104.4.1.en: 1- The greatness of God also appears in establishing the earth as though it were on foundations, as the ancients believed. By foundations God here means the stability of the earth, although the earth turns on itself every day, but by God's wisdom we do not feel this, so we live in security.

104.4.2.en: 2- The earth bears human beings, and the believers, if they stand firm in Christ the cornerstone, are not shaken.

104.5.0.en: Thou coveredst it with the deep as with a garment: the waters stood above the mountains.

104.5.1.en: 1- The waters covered everything at the beginning of creation, and God said let the dry land appear and let the waters be gathered together into one place, and He called them seas, and He called the dry land earth (Gen 1:9); that is, the earth with its mountains was covered with water, then it appeared at God's command. And the waters did not flood the earth again except in the Flood in the days of Noah, and they will not flood it again as God promised (Gen 8:21).

104.5.2.en: 2- The mountains are a symbol of the saints, the Apostles and the servants. And the waters above them are the work of the Holy Spirit in them, and His blessing upon their heads.

104.6.0.en: 7- At thy rebuke they fled; at the voice of thy thunder they hasted away. 8- They go up by the mountains; they go down by the valleys unto the place which thou hast founded for them. 9- Thou hast set a bound that they may not pass over; that they turn not again to cover the earth.

104.6.1.en: Thy thunder: God's thunder, that is, His voice, His word and His command.

104.6.4.en: 1- God commanded the waters, and they moved quickly to flood the earth with the Flood in the days of Noah, so they covered the mountains and the valleys, but after this God commanded them to withdraw, and the earth appeared again, and Noah and those with him came down from the ark. And God also reassured man by setting limits for the sea that it does not pass, so that it does not flood the earth, and even gave him a sign in the heaven, the rainbow, when the rains fall heavily and the seven colors of the spectrum appear in the sky, so that he may know that God will not flood the earth with a flood again. All this confirms the greatness and authority of God, and at the same time shows God's wrath against evil, and His love and care for His believing children.

104.6.5.en: 2- God permits trials to cover the Church in order to discipline her so that she repents, then He lifts them again, and blesses His children when they repent and rejoice in God's gifts.

104.6.6.en: 3- The verses (vv. 5-9) tell us of God's creation of the earth on the third day (Gen 1:9, 10).

104.6.7.en: God created heaven and earth for your sake, and everything on the earth for your benefit, and nothing happens except by His command, so be reassured, for He is the Upholder of all, and He is your Father who loves you and cares for you; so hold fast to His commandments, and abide in His Church, and you will enjoy fellowship with Him.

104.7.s.en: (2) God who sustains man and beast

104.7.0.en: 10- He sendeth the springs into the valleys, which run among the hills. 11- They give drink to every beast of the field:

104.7.1.en: the wild asses quench their thirst. 12- By them shall the fowls of the heaven have their habitation, which sing among the branches.

104.7.2.en: The wild asses: the wild donkey.

104.7.4.en: 1- In these following verses the writer of the Psalm tells us about God who cares for His creation, for He is not content with preparing the waters of the seas and the rivers for creation, but also makes springs of water burst forth from the underground waters that are in the earth, so they run everywhere, even among the mountains, to water not only man, but also the animals and the plants and the birds that fly above the trees and on the mountains. And He waters the tame animals and the wild animals. And when the animals drink the water they graze freely, while the birds sing on the branches, praising God who cares for them.

104.7.5.en: 2- God cares not only for man but also for the animals and the birds, so that the hearts of people may be moved to have compassion on the animals, the birds, the plants and the trees. And on the other hand, if God has compassion on the animals and the plants, He of course has compassion on the leader of creation, that is, man.

104.8.0.en: 13- He watereth the hills from his chambers: the earth is satisfied with the fruit of thy works.

104.8.1.en: 1- God waters the whole earth, even the highest thing in it, the mountains. If the rivers and springs water the valleys, God waters the mountains from His chambers, that is, the clouds, with rains. And the mountains are a symbol of the saints, whom God waters from heaven with His Holy Spirit, so they are continually filled with His grace.

104.8.2.en: 2- God's works, that is, the waters that water the plants and the trees, yield fruits with which everyone on the earth, man and animal, is satisfied. And this is a symbol of the work of the Holy Spirit in the Apostles, the priests and the servants, for He gives them His spiritual fruits, which overflow upon everyone who needs to hear the word of God, and satisfy him.

104.9.0.en: 14- He causeth the grass to grow for the cattle, and herb for the service of man: that he may bring forth food out of the earth;

104.9.1.en: 1- God cares for the food of the animals, so He gives them grass to eat, which is the fast-growing plants. As for man, who cares for farming, He gives him herbs, that is, vegetables, and also fruit, and also the crops that give bread, such as wheat, maize and barley. For God cares to satisfy all His creatures. And the meaning of this verse is found in (Ps 147:8).

104.9.2.en: 2- The bread is the word of God that satisfies our spirits, and it is Christ, incarnate in the fullness of time to redeem us and satisfy us.

104.10.0.en: 15- And wine that maketh glad the heart of man, and oil to make his face to shine, and bread which strengtheneth man's heart.

104.10.1.en: 1- God cares for man above all creatures, so He gives him bread to support him bodily, and wine also, that is, the fermented juice of the grape, whose vines were widespread in the land of the Jews, gives him health and vitality that appear in the shining of his face. And if some people drink strong wine that makes them drunk, this is a deviation that has no relation to the verse, and the Holy Bible forbids it.

104.10.2.en: 2- It is clear that the wine and the bread are a symbol of the Body and Blood of Christ, which satisfy man spiritually, so he rejoices and his face shines and his heart is glad, and he leans upon them in all his life.

104.11.0.en: 16- The trees of the Lord are full of sap; the cedars of Lebanon, which he hath planted;

104.11.1.en: 1- The trees, including the cedars of Lebanon, tall and evergreen, which God created and planted, are all satisfied with God's water and the richness of the earth, so they grow and extend to a great height, and thank God who gives them life.

104.11.2.en: 2- The cedars of Lebanon are tall trees, a symbol of the holy believers who are raised up to heaven by their many prayers. And just as the trees are evergreen, so the saints are full of spiritual life, and God has established them to be a light to the world. And they are satisfied by the overflow of the Holy Spirit upon them.

104.12.0.en: 17- Where the birds make their nests: as for the stork, the fir trees are her house.

104.12.1.en: The stork: a bird with a long beak and long legs, which flies to great heights and fights the eagle and overcomes it. It is a friend of man, and eats insects, frogs and mice from the fields. And it builds its nests at the tops of trees and on electric wires.

104.12.2.en: The fir (cypress): tall trees that grow in Lebanon, perennial and evergreen, which rival the cedar in height.

104.12.3.en: 1- Small birds, such as sparrows, or large ones, such as the stork, take refuge in the tall trees, and make a dwelling for themselves in them, and settle in them, and praise God who feeds them and provides for them their dwellings and their settling.

104.12.4.en: 2- The tall trees such as the cedar and the cypress are a symbol of the saints, to whom beginners in the spiritual life take refuge, to learn from them and cling to them; but they must rise toward heaven by their prayers, to learn the spiritual life, as the sparrows and the stork fly to the tops of the trees.

104.12.5.en: 3- The cypress is a sweet-smelling tree, evergreen and rising to heaven, and the woodworm does not eat it, so it is a symbol of the incarnate Christ, the source of life, who came down from heaven and is also without sin, so evil (the woodworm) does not come near Him.

104.13.0.en: 18- The high hills are a refuge for the wild goats; and the rocks for the conies.

104.13.1.en: The wild goats: the plural of "wa'l", the mountain goat, which is distinguished by activity and speed of movement.

104.13.2.en: The conies: a small animal that resembles the rabbit.

104.13.3.en: The wild goats can attack snakes and eat them, and therefore they dwell in the mountains and fear nothing, so God gave them strength and activity to dwell in the mountains. As for the cony, it is a weak animal that cannot dig a dwelling for itself, so it takes shelter in the rock. It is an unclean animal in the law of the Jews, like the stork, and yet God gave them to dwell in the rocks and the cypress, as Christ receives repentant sinners.

104.13.4.en: How great are Your arrangements, O God, for You give life to all Your creatures in the way that suits each kind; how much more, then, do You care for man, Your image and likeness. Therefore my soul praises You at all times, and rejoices when it sees You in Your creation and Your works, so that my heart may cling to You always.

104.14.s.en: (3) God the Creator of the sun and moon

104.14.0.en: 19- He appointed the moon for seasons: the sun knoweth his going down.

104.14.1.en: 1- This verse speaks of what God created on the fourth day, that is, the two great lights, the sun and the moon, and how by them God ordered the seasons, that is, time, with the existence of night and day through the earth's turning on itself once every day, and the seasons of the year through the earth's turning around the sun once every year. The sun knows when it will set each day, and the moon knows when it will appear each night. And by this God orders the life of man, so he works in the day and sleeps in the night.

104.14.2.en: 2- The sun is a symbol of the Sun of Righteousness, our Lord Jesus Christ, and the moon of the Church, which reflects the light of Christ the Sun of Righteousness, and so shines upon the whole world. On the other hand, the moon is also a symbol of the Jews and the Law, which prepared the way for Christ, who came in the fullness of time and knows when He will set, that is, die and redeem mankind. Therefore the spiritual person must know the source of his life, who is Christ, and cling to Him, and prepare every day for his end and for eternal life.

104.15.0.en: 20- Thou makest darkness, and it is night: wherein all the beasts of the forest do creep forth. The forest: uninhabited places, such as mountains and deserts and all abandoned places.

104.15.1.en: 1- When the sun and its light go away, night comes upon the earth, for God permits the night so that man may be calm and sleep, and on the other hand leave the works of the world and be occupied with prayer and praise.

104.15.2.en: 2- The wild beasts use the night to come out and creep and seek prey, and they are a symbol of Satan, who takes man unawares to make him fall into sin, which is symbolized by the darkness; but God protects His children who are spiritually watchful, and gives them spiritual alertness, understanding and strength, so the devil cannot overcome them. But those who forget God are in spiritual darkness and it is easy for the devil to devour them.

104.16.0.en: 21- The young lions roar after their prey, and seek their meat from God. 22- The sun ariseth, they gather themselves together, and lay them down in their dens.

104.16.1.en: Their dens: their lairs, that is, their dwelling or their holes.

104.16.2.en: Lay them down: lie down and rest.

104.16.3.en: 1- The young lions, which are the cubs of lions, move at night and give their loud voices to frighten the one they attack and devour. In this they seek their food from God, for they cannot devour except by His permission, as we see that when Daniel was cast into the den, God prevented the lions from devouring him (Dan 6:22). But when the sun rises these cubs hide in their holes.

104.16.4.en: 2- The demons work in the darkness, that is, in man's heedlessness, or when he is far from God, but when the Sun of Righteousness rises, that is, when God gives light to His children who take refuge in Him, the demons fear and flee far from them.

104.17.0.en: 23- Man goeth forth unto his work and to his labour until the evening.

104.17.1.en: 1- In the day, that is, in the light of the sun, man goes forth and does all his works until the evening, that is, at the end of the day, as Christ said, "Walk while ye have the light, lest darkness come upon you" (Jn 12:35).

104.17.2.en: 2- The day until the evening is a symbol of the whole lifetime, so man ought to use the opportunity of life to live with God and prepare for eternity, and not fear if he has fallen in the night, meaning the darkness of sin and not only the material night, but rise quickly and repent, and God receives him, and he resumes his striving with firm hope.

104.17.3.en: 3- If obstacles are found in the ministry, the priests and servants should not be troubled, but continue the preaching and the service, trusting in the power of God, which defeats the hindrances of the demons, and they gladden the heart of God by the souls that return to Him.

104.17.4.en: Remember the Resurrection of Christ at the beginning of every day to renew your activity and your vows to God, and begin with vigor a new life with Him, so pray the prayer of Prime, and set out in your spiritual life and your works and glorify God.

104.18.s.en: (4) God the Creator of the sea creatures

104.18.0.en: 24- O Lord, how manifold are thy works! in wisdom hast thou made them all: the earth is full of thy riches.

104.18.1.en: 1- God's works are great in all His creatures, because God ordered them all with wisdom, so every animal, or being, or inanimate thing is exact in its making and moves in an exact order to be in harmony with the rest of creation; all this God made with wisdom for the service of man, that he may enjoy it and that it may help him to reach God.

104.18.2.en: 2- God filled the earth with His creatures, whether the heavenly bodies, or the plants and animals on the earth, and the birds in the sky, and the animals that live in the water, whether in the seas or the rivers. For God is rich in the variety of His creatures and the multitude of His works, which dazzles man and reassures him, so he leans upon God and enjoys fellowship with Him.

104.19.0.en: 25- So is this great and wide sea, wherein are things creeping innumerable, both small and great beasts. 26- There go the ships: there is that leviathan, whom thou hast made to play therein.

104.19.1.en: Things creeping: everything that creeps on the earth, or at the bottom of the sea, or on the shore.

104.19.2.en: Leviathan: a large sea animal, whether among the animals that have become extinct or those that live now, such as the whale and the crocodile.

104.19.3.en: 1- God created the wide sea, and created in it many sea animals, large in size and small, all of which live in the water and die if they leave it. And some of them live in the water and on land, and these are the amphibians. For God is diverse in His creation and inventive in His making, and when man contemplates it he sees the greatness of God.

104.19.4.en: 2- This great, fearful sea, in which man drowns and dies if he dives into it and does not come out, yet at the same time ships can go in it freely and quickly. And the ships are a symbol of the Church, which lives in the midst of the world, but the world does not enter it by its thought. And the ships are also a symbol of the cross, which conquered Satan and bound him; for Leviathan is a symbol of Satan, who plays in the world (the sea) and fights the children of God, but he cannot attack the ships except by God's permission, just as Satan cannot conquer the Church, but on the contrary, by the power of the cross the believers in Christ tread down the power of the enemy and Satan.

104.20.0.en: 27- These wait all upon thee; that thou mayest give them their meat in due season. 28- That thou givest them they gather: thou openest thine hand, they are filled with good. 29- Thou hidest thy face, they are troubled: thou takest away their breath, they die, and return to their dust.

104.20.1.en: 1- All the animals that live in the sea, or the waters, God feeds, and they gather their food from His hand, but when God wills He ends their life, so they die, large or small, and cleave to the earth and its dust.

104.20.2.en: 2- God is the source of life for all His children, so He gives them their spiritual and bodily food, on condition that they seek Him and stretch out their hands, and He gives them, and as much as they pray they enjoy fellowship with Him. But if they go far from Him and walk in sin, He hides His face from them, and they die in their sins, since they have become carnal and earthly. And if they continue so they perish and die far from God.

104.21.0.en: 30- Thou sendest forth thy spirit, they are created: and thou renewest the face of the earth.

104.21.1.en: 1- God, who created the world of old, is He who renews life, and creates new creatures every day; for He is the giver of life, whether He creates a human being, or an animal, or a plant, for all of them are His handiwork, and consequently He must renew them, and at their head man.

104.21.2.en: 2- Man is weak and liable to fall into sins, but if he repents God renews life in him in Baptism and the sacrament of confession, and by partaking of the Body and Blood, and by the work of the Holy Spirit in him he walks in the new life and regains his way to eternal life.

104.21.3.en: Do not be troubled by the multitude of your sins, or their ugliness, because your God is able to forgive them for you and renew your life, so rise quickly to make up for what you have missed by the power of God, and complete your striving, trusting in God's support for you, until you receive your heavenly crown.

104.22.0.en: 31- The glory of the Lord shall endure for ever: the Lord shall rejoice in his works.

104.22.1.en: 1- The children of God, and all His creatures, glorify Him throughout their life on the earth, then God raises man to the Kingdom to glorify Him for ever; that is, the glorification of God is continual from now and to the age, that is, for ever.

104.22.2.en: 2- The glorification of God gladdens the heart of man, and God also rejoices in His children who praise Him; not because He needs their praise, but because He loves His children and rejoices in their salvation and their joy.

104.22.3.en: 3- God rejoiced when He created the world and said of it that it was good, and very good, and rested on the seventh day. And He also rejoiced at the completion of the redemption of mankind on the cross. And He rejoices at the repentance and salvation of His children: "joy shall be in heaven over one sinner that repenteth" (Lk 15:7). And He rejoices in the praise of His children and the submission of all creation to Him in its service to man.

104.23.0.en: 32- He looketh on the earth, and it trembleth: he toucheth the hills, and they smoke.

104.23.1.en: 1- When people on the earth sin, and God looks at them in His wrath, they are very afraid, and this great earth becomes like a leaf trembling before the wind, as the earth quaked when Christ was crucified, and when He rose from the dead (Mt 27:51). But by repentance people obtain God's forgiveness, and by redemption they obtain their new life in Him.

104.23.2.en: 2- The great mountains, which have nothing like them in strength and in height above the earth, smoke if the Lord touches them, as happened when the Lord appeared to Moses and his people on the mountain when Moses received the commandments and the Law (Ex 20:18). And however great a person becomes in position, or power, or even in the spiritual life, if he falls into pride, he smokes and trembles if God touches him in His wrath and permits him a trial. Therefore the children of God ought to live in His fear with humility, and walk in the Spirit, and so enjoy His love and care.

104.24.0.en: 33- I will sing unto the Lord as long as I live: I will sing praise to my God while I have my being.

104.24.1.en: The opportunity of life is for repentance and returning to God with all the heart, and this is the sweetest song. Then the heart opens with love, and thanks God who forgives and gives; for God satisfies the heart with His love, so it praises Him and glorifies Him all its life, until it goes forth to the Kingdom to continue its praise.

104.25.0.en: 34- My meditation of him shall be sweet: I will be glad in the Lord.

104.25.1.en: God rejoices in the repentance of His children, their prayers and their thanksgiving, and delights in their voices, as He said, "my delights were with the sons of men" (Prov 8:31). And when God rejoices He gladdens the heart of man also, so his joy in being with God increases, and he increases in praise, and He grants him spiritual gifts that cannot be expressed; he tastes something of them on earth as much as he can bear, and then wonderful things in the heavens.

104.26.0.en: 35- Let the sinners be consumed out of the earth, and let the wicked be no more. Bless thou the Lord, O my soul. Praise ye the Lord.

104.26.1.en: 1- If the children of God set out in a life of repentance and prayer and enjoyment of fellowship with God, the wicked are immersed in their sins and reject God, so nothing awaits them then but eternal torment, and they have no place with God.

104.26.2.en: 2- In view of all the works of God that this Psalm mentions, the writer of the Psalm ends his words by calling his soul to bless God and praise Him continually, and to rejoice with all the believers until it reaches the joys of eternity.

104.26.3.en: How sweet is the praise of God; for it fills the soul with peace and joy, and frees it and liberates it from the chains of the world, so it keeps away from sins, and sets out to taste the sweetness of being with God, and breathes the fragrance of eternity while it is still in the body.

104.26.4.en: God's care for His people: "O give thanks unto the Lord; call upon his name" (v. 1). Introduction:

104.26.5.en: 1- Its writer: This Psalm is one of the "orphan" Psalms that have no title, and the name of the writer is not mentioned in them, but most of the Fathers incline to the view that its writer is David. For it has the same style of writing as David, and there is not one verse that shows otherwise.

104.26.6.en: 2- When was it written? David wrote it after he brought the ark of the covenant of God back to Jerusalem (1 Chr 16:1, 7).

104.26.7.en: 3- This Psalm is counted among four Psalms that show God's promises and His faithfulness to His people throughout their history, and they are Psalms 78, 106, 136 in addition to this Psalm.

104.26.8.en: 4- This Psalm is liturgical, for it was sung at the beginnings of the months, the feast of the Dedication, and the three great feasts, the Passover, Pentecost and Tabernacles, as appears from (1 Chr 16:8-22); indeed, this chapter contains a number of the verses mentioned in this Psalm. So this Psalm was used in worship.

104.26.9.en: 5- This Psalm calls every person who believes in God to meditate on His wonderful works, so that he thanks Him and praises Him.

104.26.10.en: 6- This Psalm does not occur in the prayers of the Agpeya.
